headline: PM orders high-level committee on food safety and anti-adulteration drives
summary: A three-member panel will identify challenges faced by food safety agencies and recommend solutions within one month.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed the formation of a a three-member high-level committee to identify challenges faced by agencies responsible for ensuring safe food and conducting anti-adulteration drives.

The committee consists of Public Administration Adviser Ismail Jabiullah, State Minister for Public Administration Abdul Bari, and Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani. They are tasked with submitting a report within one month outlining immediate and long-term problems.
During a meeting at the Bangladesh Secretariat, enforcement officials from BSTI, the Bangladesh Food Safety Authority, and the Directorate of Consumer Rights briefed the PM on their struggles.
Officials highlighted a lack of manpower at the district level, the need for better laboratories and modern equipment, and the requirement for greater powers for mobile courts.
The meeting also touched upon security risks encountered by officials during drives against influential groups and syndicates.
The Prime Minister emphasized that the country must move forward despite problems and called for sincerity and responsibility from all stakeholders.
He also expressed concern over waste being thrown into lakes by educated citizens, stating that government steps alone are not enough and citizens must also show goodwill.
caption:
Food safety agencies are facing manpower shortages and security risks. The PM has now ordered a high-level panel to fix this.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed the formation of a a three-member high-level committee to identify challenges faced by agencies responsible for ensuring safe food and conducting anti-adulteration drives.

The committee consists of Public Administration Adviser Ismail Jabiullah, State Minister for Public Administration Abdul Bari, and Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani. They are tasked with submitting a report within one month outlining immediate and long-term problems.

During a meeting at the Bangladesh Secretariat, enforcement officials from BSTI, the Bangladesh Food Safety Authority, and the Directorate of Consumer Rights briefed the PM on their struggles.

Officials highlighted a lack of manpower at the district level, the need for better laboratories and modern equipment, and the requirement for greater powers for mobile courts.

The meeting also touched upon security risks encountered by officials during drives against influential groups and syndicates.

The Prime Minister emphasized that the country must move forward despite problems and called for sincerity and responsibility from all stakeholders.

He also expressed concern over waste being thrown into lakes by educated citizens, stating that government steps alone are not enough and citizens must also show goodwill.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune
